Subject: Private Offer renewal — options for unused commit and proration

Hi Stephanie,

We're starting the renewal conversations for our Azure private offer (expiring end of Nov). We have two items that need clarity before we loop procurement in for the PO: 

- We expect ~20% of the committed capacity this year will go unused because some projects were delayed. We need a path to either hand back that capacity (and reduce the next term) or have it prorated/credited against the renewal.
- If we increase commitment for FY27 (upsell), can unused units from FY26 be rolled into the first quarter of FY27 as a credit instead of a straight refund?

Attached is the draft PO your team sent last year for reference. Can you share what options Redwood supports on Marketplace private offers for capacity smoothing and proration? Timebox: procurement wants a recommended approach by Oct 15 so they can prepare their internal approvals.

Hi Helen — thanks for the heads-up and the sample PO. Short answer: yes, we can offer a couple of approaches for Azure private offers. I'll outline them below and loop in finance and marketplace ops for exact billing mechanics.

Options (high level):
1) Handback + pro rata refund: Return unused units at the end of the term; we calculate unused consumption vs commitment and issue a credit/refund or reduce the next invoice.
2) Credit rollover + upfront commitment increase: Convert unused units into a dollar credit that applies to Q1 of the new term if you commit to an increased annual amount (this preserves the Marketplace activation model).
3) Staged PO with tranches: Split the renewal into two tranches (Q1 reserve + remainder) so you only pay the up-front for what you need now; unused capacity can be shifted into tranche two with a small admin fee.

Action items for us: Dev and Marissa, can you confirm which option maps cleanly to Azure private offer paperwork (DocuSign flow + Seller PO flow) and whether we need a formal amendment vs. new private offer?

Helen — will you and Adam be available for a quick 30-min sync tomorrow (Oct 12) to agree the preferred approach before procurement drafts the PO?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Partner Sales — Redwood Inference

Quick update from ops/marketplace:
- Azure private offers: we can do an amendment that adds a credit line tied to the current private-offer ID. No need to provision a new offer if the customer keeps the same legal entity.
- Credit model: ops can create a dollar credit (not unit carryover) equal to the unused commitment value; credit can be applied to the first invoice of the next term.
- If the customer wants units carried forward instead of a dollar credit, that requires a new private offer variant; lead time ~3 weeks for approvals and marketplace listing updates.
- Billing implication: finance prefers the credit as a contra-invoice to keep ARR clean. If MedicaWorks insists on unit rollover, we need to provide a revenue impact memo to finance.

I'll attach the ops checklist and the sample amendment language I recommend.

Dev Patel
